title: Electric Can Openers for Stiff or Sore Hands: Four Countertop Models and What They Cost
subtitle: A plain-English look at four countertop electric can openers, what the makers say they do, and the hand tasks they still leave to you.
excerpt: If a hand-crank can opener has become hard on your hands, a countertop electric model may be worth a look. Here are four current models from $25.99 to $44.99, and what they can and cannot do.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: A can of soup should not feel like a puzzle. But for many people with stiff fingers, sore wrists or arthritis, a hand-crank can opener asks for exactly the motions that hurt most: a tight pinch to clamp it on, then turn after turn of a small knob.

An electric can opener uses a small motor in place of the cranking. It is a modest gadget at a modest price, and it may suit some kitchens better than a manual opener. It will not do everything, though, and this guide is clear about where it stops.
All four models here are countertop openers that plug into an outlet. Each maker's product page describes its own design, so the details differ from model to model.
The Black+Decker has a one-touch lever that releases the can once it is open. Its page says the can spins in place on a stable base, and that the cutting assembly is removable for cleaning.

The two SmoothTouch models from Hamilton Beach cut along the side of the can, which the maker says leaves a smooth lid with no sharp edge. Both have a push-down opening lever. The OpenStation lists automatic shutoff for hands-free operation, along with a washable, twist-off cutting lever.

It helps to be clear about the limits. Lining up the can is still a hand task. One customer review on the Black+Decker page says it "works quickly once you get the can in the correct spot," which is a reminder that placing the can takes some hand control. These openers need counter space near an outlet. None of the four is cordless or battery powered, and none is a motorized jar opener.

items: Can types: pop-top and regular-can handling differs by model, so confirm the model covers the cans you buy before ordering.
Edge style: the SmoothTouch pages say they cut along the side and leave no sharp edge on the lid, which may matter if you worry about cuts.
Automatic shutoff: the OpenStation page lists it as a feature for hands-free operation.
Cleaning: the Black+Decker has a removable cutting assembly and the OpenStation has a washable, twist-off cutting lever. Check how each model cleans before you buy.
Base: the Black+Decker page describes a wide stabilizing base for most can sizes.
Counter space and an outlet: measure your spot first, since all four are corded countertop appliances. Sizes are listed on each product page.
Warranty and returns: the Black+Decker lists a 2-year limited warranty. Check the warranty and return policy for any model before you order.

Shipping: Hamilton Beach lists free shipping at $49.99 and Black+Decker at $99. The priciest opener here is $44.99, so a single Hamilton Beach opener would not reach its threshold. Shipping fees were not checked.

sections.content: Setting it up and using it well
Choose a spot near an outlet where the opener can sit steady on the counter. The OpenStation has built-in cord storage, which can help keep the extra cord out of the way.

Read the manual before the first can. The Black+Decker page links a product manual PDF, and the Hamilton Beach 76607G page links a use-and-care guide. Practice on an ordinary can before you try an oddly shaped one.
For the 76606FG, the Hamilton Beach product page says: "An easy push down lever makes quick work of removing both pop-top and regular cans." The page for the 76607G lists the same design.

A note on prices: only the list prices posted on each product page in November 2026 were checked. None of the four pages shows a subscription or monthly fee. Replacement parts and shipping costs were not verified, and prices can change.
An electric can opener is a kitchen helper, not a treatment. If hand pain or stiffness is getting in the way of daily tasks, talk with your doctor.
sections.label: Good to Know

sections.content: If you are shopping for a parent, it can help to ask which cans they buy most and where they would like the opener to sit. Then compare the product pages together.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER Easy Cut Extra Tall Electric Can Opener (EC500B-T)
products.blurb: The lowest-priced of the four, with a one-touch lever that releases the can once it is open and a wide stabilizing base for most can sizes. It includes a removable multi-tool for bottle caps and pop-tops and a 2-year limited warranty.

products.name: Hamilton Beach OpenStation Can Opener with Tools (76382FJ)
products.blurb: Suits someone who likes the idea of automatic shutoff for hands-free operation, as the page puts it. It also includes a multi-tool for hard plastic packages, pop-tops and bottles, plus two manual jar-opener attachments.

products.name: Hamilton Beach SmoothTouch Can Opener (76606FG)
products.blurb: A fit for anyone who worries about cuts: the page says it cuts along the side, leaving a smooth lid with no sharp edge. It opens both regular and pop-top cans with a push-down lever.

products.name: Hamilton Beach SmoothTouch Can Opener with Scissors (76607G)
products.blurb: The same cut-along-the-side design and easy-touch lever as the 76606FG, with scissors that store in the back of the opener.
